native_home: Marketplace tiles, ad units, carousels, legacy IG feed
communicates: Neutral, product-first, systematic — a catalogue page
consequence: No dominant axis, so symmetry or centring wins. A thirds offset is only 16.7% of width from centre and reads as a mistake rather than a choice
anchor_rule: Product optical centre on frame centre

native_home: Meta feed — the ratio Meta itself recommends; IG portrait post
communicates: Human, editorial, mobile-first. The most feed area available without being a Story
consequence: A vertical subject fits whole and still leaves a real copy band of 20–25% of height
anchor_rule: Subject eyes on the upper thirds line

native_home: IG profile-grid thumbnail since Jan 2025; native 3:4 photo support added May 2025
communicates: Same reading as 4:5, one notch taller
consequence: Creates the double-crop trap: a 4:5 upload shows uncropped in feed and loses 6.25% of its width on the profile grid
anchor_rule: Keep logos and edge-critical marks at least 7% of width inside the left and right edges

communicates: Discovery, editorial, a thing worth saving
consequence: Tall enough for a text lockup above a whole product without either being cramped
anchor_rule: Product base on the lower thirds line and lockup above it

communicates: Formal, still-life, a plate rather than a photograph
consequence: Nearly square, so it behaves like 1:1: symmetry-friendly and hostile to a weak offset
anchor_rule: Hero on centre; use symmetry deliberately rather than by default

communicates: Classic photographic, documentary — shot by a photographer
consequence: Wide enough that the dynamic-symmetry eye leaves the thirds line: 30.8% of width against 33.3%

native_home: YouTube, web hero, in-stream, TV, presentations
consequence: Large horizontal negative space is cheap here, and it becomes a letterbox strip in a phone feed
anchor_rule: Subject edge on the 24% vertical rather than 33%

consequence: A wider 16:9 that behaves the same way; no new problem and no new benefit
anchor_rule: Subject edge on the computed eye vertical

native_home: Ultrawide display, some AI model presets
consequence: Extreme: either the hero is small or the frame has to be built in layers
anchor_rule: Hero small and off-axis; do not try to fill the width with one object

native_home: Cinema scope — the DCI 2K Scope container is exactly 2048 x 858
consequence: The widest ratio that still reads as a film. The eye sits at 14.9% of width, so subjects go near the edges
Platform interface eats the top and bottom, leaving about 42% of the frame usable, and the optical centre moves to 39.5% of height
anchor_rule: Eyes and hero centroid at 38–42% of frame height and 1–3% left of centre

label: root-2 (A4)
native_home: Print — ISO 216 paper. A4 is 210 x 297 mm and 297/210 = 1.4143
communicates: Official, printed, filed — a document rather than a post
consequence: Halves into two identical root-2 rectangles, which is why a folded leaflet keeps its proportion. It is also the one ratio where the two grids agree exactly: h squared = 2 w squared makes the dynamic-symmetry eye land on 1/3 to within a rounding error, so on ISO paper thirds and dynamic symmetry are the same grid and there is nothing to argue about
anchor_rule: Trim margin first: nothing that must survive enters the outer 60 px, because a guillotine does not forgive an edge

label: phi 1.618:1
native_home: Not a delivery ratio. A sizing ratio: type scale, margin-to-column, image-to-copy split
communicates: Nothing to a viewer. It is a generator for consistent sizes, not a signal
consequence: Removing the square from a golden rectangle leaves a golden rectangle, which is the whole of its usefulness
anchor_rule: Use 61.8 / 38.2 to split image against copy or to build a type scale; never as a placement rule
